cards.back: Everything the assistant may search: source documents, cleaned and chunked copies, their metadata and the indexes built over them.
Each layer is rebuildable from the one before, so you can change parsing or chunking without re-downloading millions of files through rate-limited APIs.
Knowledge base: facts that change, need citations or have access rules. Fine-tuning: format, tone, vocabulary, a narrow repeated task.
What one user said or prefers across sessions, not shared company knowledge.
Keep headings, lists and tables: they drive chunking and give each chunk its heading path.
Hash normalised content so five copies of a policy become one document with five locations; otherwise duplicates fill the top results.
Split on sections, then paragraphs, then sentences until under the size limit. The sensible default for mixed content.
300 to 800 tokens with 10 to 20% overlap, each prefixed with its title and heading path so it stands alone.
doc_id, chunk_id, version, source and URL, title and heading path, updated_at, author, space, type, region or language, allowed_principals and embedding_model_version.
Webhooks for speed, a periodic reconciliation crawl for correctness; process each changed doc as a unit and delete chunks from old versions.
Ingestion lag (edit to searchable), documents failing to parse, and coverage (source docs vs catalog docs).

quiz.q: A company wants an assistant that answers from policies that change monthly and must cite sources. Which approach?
quiz.why: RAG fits facts that change, need citations or have access rules.

quiz.q: Why is fine-tuning on company documents a poor way to add knowledge?
choices: It bakes in facts that go stale and ignores permissions
It is always cheaper than RAG
quiz.why: Fine-tuning is for style and narrow tasks, not fresh, permissioned facts.

quiz.q: Which chunking strategy is the sensible default for mixed content?
quiz.why: Recursive splitting respects structure while keeping chunks under the limit.

quiz.q: Why prefix each chunk with "Leave policy > India > Parental leave"?
choices: So the chunk stands alone with its context
To hide it from keyword search
quiz.why: The heading path gives an isolated chunk its context.

quiz.q: Which metadata field makes permission filtering possible?
quiz.why: The access control list is stored on each chunk as allowed_principals.

quiz.q: Why keep the raw downloaded copies?
choices: To re-parse or re-chunk without hitting source APIs again
They are required for citations UI
quiz.why: Every layer rebuilds from the one before it.
